analysis: The trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5275, exceeding the stated 0.505 hypothesis threshold by 0.0225. Category HR@10 was 0.580 for Movies_and_TV, 0.605 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.410 for Electronics, and 0.515 for CDs_and_Vinyl. These results support recurrent state modeling as a useful hypothesis; they do not isolate whether the GRU, BPR-max loss, or other training choices caused the improvement. Electronics remains the weakest category. No test results were available.
code_summary: Trains one independent network per category using seed 42: a two-layer, 128-dimensional GRU over up to 64 purchases, with shared input/output item embeddings, dropout, LayerNorm, a linear output projection, and jointly learned item biases. BPR-max training uses 256 shared sampled negatives, masks purchases in the training window, and adds a negative-score penalty. AdamW, gradient clipping, validation-based learning-rate reduction, and early stopping control optimization. Each category retains one validation-selected checkpoint. The generated predictor embeds the matching architecture, routes by dataset name, and scores candidates from the last nonpadding recurrent state. Supplied splits remain unchanged; no ensembles or separately fitted auxiliary scorers are used.
